title: A security caller asks for the login code
mechanism_summary: An impostor claims there is an account security problem and requests a verification code. Sharing it can give the attacker the second credential needed to enter the account.
suggested_beats: A caller offers urgent protection.
Protection requires reading out a code.
Contact the provider independently.
why_it_works: The promise of protection disguises a request for account access.

title: Payroll login hidden in a search advertisement
mechanism_summary: A fraudulent search advertisement leads to a lookalike payroll portal that captures login credentials. Attackers use access to change deposit instructions and divert funds.
suggested_beats: An employee searches for payroll access.
The apparent portal collects credentials.
Use a saved official login address.
why_it_works: A prominent search result can be mistaken for a verified destination.

title: A second approver is drawn into the same trap
mechanism_summary: After capturing corporate login details, attackers may ask a second authorized person to use the fraudulent website. This undermines a payment process meant to require two independent approvals.
suggested_beats: A corporate login appears to need help.
The second approver enters the same trap.
Verify the destination before approving.
why_it_works: A routine approval workflow can lend credibility to a compromised process.

title: A swapped SIM receives the security texts
mechanism_summary: A scammer convinces a mobile provider to move a person's number to another SIM. Combined with login credentials, intercepted verification texts allow access to linked accounts.
suggested_beats: The phone unexpectedly loses service.
Security codes reach someone else.
Contact the carrier through a trusted channel.
why_it_works: Trust in a familiar phone number hides the change in who controls it.

title: The inbox becomes a password-reset gateway
mechanism_summary: An intruder who controls an email account requests resets for other accounts. The reset links arrive in the compromised inbox, allowing further lockouts.
suggested_beats: An email account is compromised.
Other account passwords begin changing.
Secure the inbox and review account recovery settings.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone using email for account recovery
why_it_works: The convenience of centralized recovery also concentrates access in one inbox.

title: A hidden forwarding rule survives unnoticed
mechanism_summary: An email intruder adds a rule that forwards incoming messages elsewhere. Private correspondence can continue reaching the intruder until the unauthorized rule is removed.
suggested_beats: An intruder accesses the inbox.
A hidden rule copies incoming mail.
Review forwarding rules during account recovery.
why_it_works: Invisible settings can conceal continuing exposure after obvious symptoms disappear.

title: A real verification page authorizes the wrong device
mechanism_summary: A phishing email supplies a device code and directs the recipient to a genuine verification page. Entering the attacker's code authorizes access to the recipient's cloud account.
suggested_beats: A document-sharing email supplies a code.
The code connects an attacker's device.
Do not authorize device codes from unsolicited messages.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone opening a shared work document
why_it_works: A genuine website can make an attacker-initiated authorization seem safe.

title: Old breach credentials unlock another account
mechanism_summary: Attackers obtain login credentials exposed in earlier breaches. They use those credentials to gain unauthorized account access and pursue money or information.
suggested_beats: Old login details circulate after a breach.
An attacker uses them against an account.
Use unique passwords and enable stronger authentication.
why_it_works: Reusing a familiar password lets one breach threaten several accounts.
